facade_owner.reason: internal/service imports internal/httpapi and net/http, while a new application package can own typed use cases and leave HTTP, MCP, Wails, Flutter, and the C ABI as adapters
first_slice: context cancellation and closed application errors

sqlite_owner.selected: checksum-pinned upstream SQLite amalgamation with cgo
sqlite_owner.reason: the pinned amalgamation passed the unchanged real schema-v27 store, snapshot, and sync code on Linux and Android; modernc passed SQL/file compatibility but would require replacing 43 direct-C store files, is larger and heavier in the measured workload, embeds SQLite 3.53.3 instead of current 3.53.4, and does not list Android as an upstream-supported target
runtime_options: SQLite Online Backup API for physical snapshots
sqlite_owner.update_policy: H1 vendors only sqlite3.c, sqlite3.h, the public-domain notice, and a provenance manifest. Every SQLite update is a dedicated reviewed slice: verify the official SHA3-256, record SHA-256 and source ID, diff compile options, rerun desktop and API-35 store/snapshot/sync tests, rerun both ABI forms and symbol checks, rerun the checkpointed round-trip and cost matrix, refresh licenses, and retain the previous pin for rollback until release acceptance passes.
sqlite_owner.rollback: Before release acceptance, revert the vendored pin/build wiring and retain the existing pkg-config desktop adapter. Canonical databases remain ordinary schema-v27 SQLite files; never change engines while a file is open, and checkpoint WAL before handing a file to a rollback build.

abi.primary_build_form: c-shared for Flutter/Dart FFI and dynamic desktop hosts
abi.secondary_build_form: c-archive as a validated static-embedding option, not the default Android package
abi.dispatch: one bounded typed JSON operation surface; bulk bytes use streams
abi.ownership: inputs are caller-owned and copied before return; outputs are immutable C allocations released exactly once; C-visible memory contains no Go pointers
abi.handles: unsigned 64-bit opaque generation-bearing handles; zero, stale, wrong-kind, and foreign-instance handles are refused
abi.threads: host calls may enter on host threads; Go never invokes a host callback from an arbitrary Go thread; completions and events are polled
abi.shutdown: close marks the live instance shutting down, refuses new calls and streams, cancels and joins owned work, invalidates handles, then becomes idempotent for that generation
abi.host_probe: passed c-shared, c-archive, generated headers, exact symbols, ownership, cancel, poll, events, streams, and shutdown
abi.android_x86_64_probe: passed the same C host against an NDK API-35 c-shared library
abi.real_store_link_probe: passed schema-v27 bootstrap through c-shared with SQLite 3.53.4, no dynamic SQLite dependency, and no exported sqlite3_* symbols
abi.dlclose_policy: not a lifecycle primitive; hosts close all instances and streams before process teardown

canonical_file_owner.policy: exactly one Go application-core instance and exactly one embedded SQLite engine own a canonical database file
canonical_file_owner.same_process: canonicalize the database identity before open and refuse a second live instance in the application registry
canonical_file_owner.cross_process: hold a nonblocking exclusive owner sidecar lock for the full store lifetime and refuse open when it is held
canonical_file_owner.non_cooperating_clients: do not link Room, Jetpack SQLite, a second sqlite3, or any Flutter SQLite plugin into the canonical-file path
canonical_file_owner.negative_probe: passed: first owner acquired; second cooperating owner exited 3 with Resource temporarily unavailable
canonical_file_owner.symbol_probe: passed: real-store shared libraries had no libsqlite3 dependency and exported no sqlite3_* symbols
canonical_file_owner.production_status: policy selected and prototyped; enforcement belongs to H1

concurrency_wal_and_crash.connection: one store owner, FULLMUTEX opens, existing Go store serialization, and a 5-second busy timeout
concurrency_wal_and_crash.wal: WAL is canonical during live use; a TRUNCATE checkpoint and clean close precede raw file transfer; snapshots use the Online Backup API instead of copying a live main file
concurrency_wal_and_crash.shutdown_order: refuse new work, cancel calls/jobs, close streams, join workers, checkpoint/close SQLite, release the owner lock, invalidate the generation
crash_recovery_evidence: sync admission restart and injected pre-commit failure passed on API-35
uncommitted canonical and sync-operation rows rolled back on close on API-35
sanitized SQLite snapshot creation passed on API-35
desktop store/snapshot/sync package suites passed against the pin

android_target.second_runtime_abi_effect: H8 must add a physical or emulated arm64 run of the same ABI, store, snapshot, sync, ownership, and package matrix before arm64 production support is claimed. Until then x86_64/API-35 is the only runtime evidence and arm64-v8a is build-only.

modernc_sqlite.license: BSD-3-Clause plus SQLite public-domain notice; optional sqlite-vec sources carry MIT

desktop_sqlite_ab.interpretation: The small process-level workload includes startup and adapter overhead and is not a product-wide latency guarantee. On this run modernc built faster, while the C executable ran faster and used less RSS and disk.

modernc.real_store_suite: not run because the current store has 43 direct-C implementation files and no modernc adapter

sequence: desktop SQLite 3.53.4 created and checkpointed 1000-note FTS5/JSON/WAL database
Android modernc SQLite 3.53.3 verified it and added note 1001
Android checkpointed and closed the file
pulled file hash matched the emulator hash
desktop SQLite 3.53.4 verified integrity, WAL, 1001 notes, and the exact modernc row

limitations: H0 did not land production internal/application or the ABI-major-1 library; H1 owns that integration.
The lifecycle ABI probe and the real-store shared-link probe are separate disposable binaries; H1 must join them and run semantic REST/ABI parity.
modernc did not run the real Notrios store, snapshot, or sync suite because doing so requires a 43-file adapter rewrite; its SQL/file compatibility and Android runtime were measured instead.
The A/B corpus is synthetic and small; results are selection evidence on this machine, not universal performance guarantees.
Only API-35 x86_64 ran. Android arm64 is build-only; physical devices, other API levels, iOS, Windows, and macOS are not runtime claims.
The owner lock is a cooperating-owner prototype, not production enforcement against an arbitrary external SQLite client.
No concurrent cross-engine access was attempted because the selected policy forbids it and SQLite documents that separately linked copies can corrupt locking state.
